prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right one depends on your location in the Phoenix area, the exact problem, your budget, whether you need emergency service, and whether you want a national chain or a local shop. I can help you find highly rated options near you if you tell me your zip code or neighborhood. Meanwhile, here’s a quick guide to pick the best contractor for your AC repair:

Questions I need
- Where in Phoenix are you (zip code or neighborhood)?
- Residential or commercial system?
- What’s wrong (no cool air, blowing hot air, noisy, leaking, frozen coils, smells, etc.)?
- Is it an emergency (no cooling during a heatwave)?
- Any brand/model or warranty still active?

How to choose a good HVAC company
- Licensing and insurance: Verify they’re licensed by the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) and carry liability insurance.
- Technician credentials: Look for NATE-certified techs or manufacturer certifications for your brand.
- Local reputation: Check recent Google and Yelp reviews, plus the BBB profile.
- Transparent pricing: They should give a clear estimate and explain diagnostic fees.
- Warranty & guarantees: Ask about parts/labor warranties and satisfaction guarantees.
- Experience with your equipment: Make sure they service your system’s brand/type.
- Availability: Same‑day or emergency service if that’s needed.

Questions to ask a contractor
- Are you licensed and insured? What’s your ROC number?
- Do you have references or recent customer reviews in my area?
- Are your technicians NATE-certified?
- What’s the diagnostic fee and is it applied to the repair?
- What’s the estimated timeline and warranty on parts/labor?
- Will you provide the estimate in writing?

Quick troubleshooting you can try now
- Check/change the air filter.
- Make sure the thermostat is set to “cool” and the temperature is below room temp.
- Check the breaker panel and the outdoor unit disconnect.
- If the outdoor unit is iced over, turn the system off and call a tech (running it frozen can damage the compressor).

If you give me your zip code and a short description of the problem I’ll list 3–5 well-reviewed companies near you (with pros/cons) and help you pick one.
